MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
August 19, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Monday,
August 19, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Traina led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Attorney King, Public Works Director Damasse, Community Services Director
McPherron, Parks and Recreation Director Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

3.  SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Councilmember Gazeley presented certificates of recognition to the 2013 Lomita Little League
Board of Directors, as well as a check in the amount of $1,000 in support of the Lomita Little
League.

Presentation of the Annual Report for the Railroad Museum Foundation Board by
Chairperson Susie Dever.

Susie Dever, Chairperson of the Railroad Museum Foundation Board, stated that since 2012,
the main focus of the Railroad Museum Foundation Board has been to build-up attendance at
the Museum and to increase the “Friends of Museum” membership. Chairperson Dever
announced that the Board had established an annual event calendar, which features Speaker
Forums, High Tea, a Wine Tasting, and Community Events.

Chairperson Dever reported that Railroad Museum Foundation Board had applied for and
received funding from two grants in 2011, and the Board has recently applied for another grant
through Union Pacific to update signage and provide for other upgrades to the Museum.
According to Chairperson Dever, some additional past year efforts have also included
relationship-building with other community organizations, and updating the Museum’s website.

  Page 1
 Furthermore, Chairperson Dever stated that the Board had drafted a photographic policy that
will be presented to City Council for consideration at a later date.

Chairperson Dever requested that Council consider increasing the membership of the Railroad
Museum Foundation Board from five to seven members. Furthermore, Chairperson Dever
asked that Council consider funding for secure and on-site storage for the Museum collection,
as well as funding for additional enclosed space so that the Museum could host larger groups.

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that based on a number of recent articles
there is a lot of discussion regarding the water supply in Southern California. According to City
Manager Rock, the primary concern is that the ongoing drought will continue, which in turn
would affect the water supply from the Colorado River, and currently Southern California
receives 66% of imported water. City Manager Rock stated that the Governor has proposed a
tunnel water delivery system in order to preserve the Delta ecosystem and allow for
uninterrupted water distribution to both Central and Southern California; however, this project
would take about 20 years to build.

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

David Popelka, Planning Commissioner, asked that City Council consider directing staff to
update the General Plan.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Sanchez stated that after reviewing the data provided by staff regarding the
overhead cost charged to the Water Fund, it seems as if the General Fund is subsidizing those
costs; therefore, Councilmember Sanchez requested a future agenda item to discuss the
overhead costs charged to the Water Fund. Councilmembers Gazeley, Savidan, and Traina
agreed to place this request on a future agenda for discussion.

Councilmember Savidan reported that he attended the Sister City fundraising event, which was
well attended, and that the exchange students from Japan had a wonderful time. Furthermore,
Councilmember Savidan thanked Mayor Estrada and the other members of the Sister City
organization for all their efforts.

Councilmember Gazeley stated that there are now 13 new human cases of the West Nile Virus,
with the majority of them being in the South Bay; Councilmember Gazeley asked residents to
take precautions against the West Nile Virus.

Mayor Estrada stated that the Sister City Farewell Party was well attended, and noted that the
exchange students had a very busy schedule and a wonderful time.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  Page 2
   a. Motion to Waive Further Reading.

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting held on
  August 5, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands.

  PUBLIC HEARING:

5. CONGESTION MANAGEMENT PLAN (CMP)

An annual review of the City of Lomita’s conformance with the Congestion Management
Program (CMP) for Los Angeles County, and the adoption of the CMP Local Development
Report by Resolution.

Principal Planner Velasco stated that State law requires an annual review of the activities within
each city that add to or act to relieve traffic congestion, or otherwise adversely affect traffic in
the City. Ms. Velasco went on to outline the development projects completed in the City over
the last year. Furthermore, Ms. Velasco stated that Council must adopt a Resolution approving
the Congestion Management Plan Local Development Report by September 1, 2013, and failure
to do so may affect future gas taxes, as well as other state and federal transportation funding.

Councilmember Sanchez stated that he had reviewed the entire report and that Chapter 89
requires a bi-annual traffic count to be completed on City streets. Councilmember Sanchez
asked if staff had conducted the traffic count, to which Ms. Velasco responded that the County
handles that task for the City, and added that the Congestion Management Plan is more like a
reference tool while the County studies the feasibility of the congestion mitigation fee.

Councilmember Sanchez stated that based on the report, the Pacific Coast Highway does not
meet the required standards, and in turn he could not support the adoption of the proposed
resolution. Discussion followed on the possible effects of not passing the resolution.

Mayor Estrada opened the Public Hearing. There were no speakers. Mayor Estrada closed the
Public Hearing.

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve staff’s recommendation to approve the proposed
resolution. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion.

In response to Councilmember Traina’s question regarding what would happen if the proposed
resolution is not approved, Ms. Velasco stated that the City needs to adopt the resolution by
September 1, 2013, or the gas taxes could potentially be jeopardized.

Councilmember Sanchez stated that in the report it says that the State Controller could provide
an extension to the City in order to make sure that the requirements are met.

Councilmember Savidan suggested that the City submit the report, and if the requirements are
not met, then the State Controller would send the report back, and the City could make the
necessary revisions at that time.

ROLL CALL:

  Page 3
 AYES: Councilmembers Gazeley, Traina, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada
NOES: Councilmember Sanchez.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS:

6. FIGTREE PACE PROGRAM

Discussion/consideration of resolutions that would allow commercial property owners within the
City of Lomita to participate in the FIGTREE PACE Program.

Principal Planner Velasco provided an overview of the FIGTREE PACE Program and stated that
Assembly Bills 811 and 474, which were passed in 2010, authorize cities and counties to
designate an area within which property owners may enter into contractual assessments to
finance the installation of conservation improvements to their property. According to Ms.
Velasco, the FIGTREE PACE Program is similar to the HERO Program that City Council
approved earlier in the month.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the resolutions per staff’s recommendation.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion.

Councilmember Traina expressed his concern as to whether the City has the necessary
infrastructure to accommodate all the electrical vehicles, to which Ms. Velasco responded that
Southern California Edison, in conjunction with the South Bay Cities Council of Governments, is
currently working on the electrical vehicle infrastructure plan.

The motion carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned in memory of Georgia Zabel at 7:55 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
